findings.title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
findings.body: The deleteMany uses OR: [{method:SMS, scheduledDate lte now}, {retryCount gt 1}]. The second branch has no method filter and no scheduled:false filter, so any WorkflowReminder with retryCount>1 is deleted even if method is EMAIL/WHATSAPP or even if scheduled:true with a future scheduledDate and valid Twilio referenceId. That causes data loss and orphaned scheduled sends that can no longer be cancelled. It should be ANDed with method: SMS and scheduled:false.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses counts
findings.body: Both failure paths do data:{retryCount: reminder.retryCount+1} using the value read at the start of the cron run (lines 184 and 195). Overlapping cron executions read the same stale value and overwrite each other, losing a retry and allowing infinite retries. Use atomic update data:{retryCount:{increment:1}} instead.

findings.title: Missing sendTo/message never increments retryCount
findings.body: If message is empty or sendTo is falsy the if (message?.length && sendTo) block does nothing and falls through without updating retryCount or scheduled. Such reminders, e.g. missing/invalid smsReminderNumber, are refetched every cron run until scheduledDate passes, defeating the stated goal of deleting after 2 failures. The failure/skip path must also increment retryCount or otherwise resolve the reminder.
